verdicts.note: No abstract; 'Infrastructure and the American Family: MATERIAL CONDITIONS, HOUSEHOLD STRUCTURE, and the Visibility Gap, 1973-2024'. Names material conditions and household structure together over fifty years; Wall 1 territory. Trace.
No abstract; sons and voting in Chinese village elections.
Measurement of fertility preferences and their intergenerational transmission. A.19's.
Female labour force participation and fertility in developing countries. C.2.e's.

No abstract; 'Continuing the Family Lineage? PRIMARY FAMILY MEMBERS' traditional fertility VALUES and FERTILITY in rural China'. The in-laws' preferences as the exposure, which is the extended arm's mechanism at the decision level. Trace.
Birth order and child nutrition in Kyrgyzstan, in a setting characterised by WIDESPREAD MULTIGENERATIONAL CO-RESIDENCE. The arrangement is context, the outcome is child nutrition.
Differentiation of fertility attitudes in Shandong under the two-child policy.
Essays in labor and public economics on access to public goods.
Scoping review of intergenerational relationships and mental health among older Chinese adults, with co-residence among the exposures.
Data table for the Shandong fertility-attitudes study.

LABOUR MIGRATION and HOUSEHOLD STRUCTURE in Tajikistan 2012-2023. Male out-migration as a driver of household composition in a poor remittance economy -- a driver-to-arrangement link in a setting the frame reaches nowhere else.
Population ageing, living arrangements and inequality measurement in Korea.

No abstract; 'HOUSING CAREERS AND DEMOGRAPHIC CHANGE: Life Courses, Inequality, and INTERGENERATIONAL HOUSING FUTURES'. Wall 1's framing with the intergenerational dimension named in the title. Trace for the second-read packet.

Fertility desire and first-birth intentions among childless partnered adults in SPAIN, a country marked by DELAYED LIFE-COURSE TRANSITIONS and persistent gaps between aspirations and outcomes. The registered setting and the intention outcome; the arrangement is background rather than exposure.

REGRESSION DISCONTINUITY at the RETIREMENT THRESHOLD on time allocation and ADULT CHILDREN'S FERTILITY. Another well-identified grandparental-time design; C.2.a's exposure, and now the fourth pension or retirement discontinuity in this frame.
Banking and fintech in Japan's ageing economy.

No abstract; son preference, INTERGENERATIONAL HOUSEHOLD DYNAMICS and women's MENTAL HEALTH in India, Journal of Development Economics. The extended configuration with a wellbeing outcome; economics-journal identification standards make it worth tracing.
Journal issue contents including household formation among the topics.
Market transition, patrilineal inheritance beliefs and son preference in China. D.2.c's.
Joint taxation and couples' labour supply.
OLG model in which child allowance interacts with GRANDPARENTAL CHILDCARE and interest rates. C.2.a's exposure, formal.

ELDERLY PENSION POLICY and grandchildren's NUTRITION in MULTIGENERATIONAL households in Nepal. Identified pension variation and the multigenerational household as the setting; the outcome is child nutrition.

NUCLEARIZATION of the family across INDIA, PAKISTAN, BANGLADESH AND NEPAL over three decades of DHS data, with rapid nuclearisation in India and Nepal and persistent joint families in Pakistan. The South Asian exposure series, and the divergence within the region is itself the within-setting variation Wall 3 wants.

Community networks and satisfaction with the child-rearing environment in a Japanese city, against the SHIFT AWAY FROM THREE-GENERATION CO-RESIDENCE. The exposure trend is the premise; the outcome is satisfaction.
Editorial on assistive technology for older adults.
No abstract; family formation under a subjective future constraint. D.3.c-adjacent.
No abstract; marriage without births among Chinese and Korean Americans.
No abstract; fertility and intergenerational health effects of China's two-child policy.
Teachers' adaptation to witchcraft beliefs in Tanzania.

No abstract; 'GRANDPARENTAL SUPPORT AND THE MARGINS OF FERTILITY INTENTIONS: Evidence from the 2018 SPANISH FERTILITY SURVEY'. C.2.a's exposure by the standing rule, but it is in the registered setting and on a fertility-intention outcome, so it is a boundary case worth tracing.
Self-published manuscript proposing 'collapse demography' as a field.
Distillation across post-trained large language models. Matched on 'families' of models.
